As far as I know RFID cards are actually not crazy common any more and people are starting to phase them out because of the enormous risk. At least in the US.

For those that don't know or didn't read the article, they're talking about the cards you tap against the card reader and don't swipe or insert at all. Thieves can use modified scanners to scan them from inside your pocket. That's why you see people marketing RFID blocking wallets now, for these cards and other cards that carry RFID chips.

I still see the pads everywhere but I never see anyone use them.

If you have one just get a metal card holder, most fit in your wallet and almost all will block scanners.
A lot of the time a special scanner isn't even required just a cellphone with NFC capabilities.
